subproblem.title: The measure θHⁿ⌞M: finite on compacts, same null sets as Hⁿ⌞M, and weighted tangent planes are tangent planes with multiplicity θ(x)
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (M : Set (Rn N)) (θ : Rn N → ℝ) (μ : Measure (Rn N)), NullMeasurableSet M μHE[n] → IsPositiveLocallyIntegrableWeight n M θ → μ = ((μHE[n] : Measure (Rn N)).restrict M).withDensity (fun z ↦ ENNReal.ofReal (θ z)) → (∀ K : Set (Rn N), IsCompact K → μ K < ∞) ∧ (∀ S : Set (Rn N), μ S = 0 ↔ μHE[n] (M ∩ S) = 0) ∧ ∀ (x : Rn N) (P : Submodule ℝ (Rn N)), HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x P → HasApproxTangentPlaneWithMultiplicity n μ x P (θ x)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 5 of the parent proof ('From weighted tangent planes to tangent measures'). It realises the measure θHⁿ⌞M of Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(1) and Theorem 1.9 (chapter-03.txt lines 298-323) together with the blow-up scaling of Definition 1.7. It uses the sibling child setIntegral_blowUpMap_image, called (A) below: ∫_{η_{x,r}(A)} g dHⁿ = (rⁿ)⁻¹∫_A g∘η_{x,r} dHⁿ for every r > 0, every set A and every g.

Setting. Fix n, N, M, θ and μ as in the statement, and substitute μ = ν.withDensity w, where ν := Hⁿ⌞M and w(z) := ofReal(θ(z)) ∈ [0, ∞). The positive weight hypothesis gives (i) θ(z) > 0 for z ∈ M, (ii) θ is ν-a.e. measurable, and (iii) θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K.

Remark on the parent's θ'. The parent used a Borel θ' = θ ν-a.e. Since ofReal∘θ' = w ν-a.e., the two densities define the same measure (withDensity_congr_ae), so we work with θ directly.

0. Preliminaries.
   - w is ν-a.e. measurable (ofReal is continuous and θ is ν-a.e. measurable) and w(z) < ∞ for every z.
   - For z ∈ M, w(z) = ofReal(θ(z)) > 0, and w(z).toReal = θ(z) because θ(z) ≥ 0.
   - M is Hⁿ-null-measurable, so ν-a.e. z lies in M (ae_restrict_mem₀), and ν(T) = Hⁿ(T ∩ M) for every set T (Measure.restrict_apply₀').

1. (a) Local finiteness. Let K be compact. K is closed, hence Borel, so μ(K) = ∫_K w dν (withDensity_apply) = ∫_{K∩M} ofReal(θ) dHⁿ (restrict_restrict, using K Borel). By (iii), θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ K, so ∫_{M∩K} ofReal(θ) dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M∩K} |θ| dHⁿ < ∞ (Integrable.lintegral_lt_top). Hence μ(K) < ∞.

2. (b) Null sets. Let S ⊆ ℝ^N be any set.
   - Since w is ν-a.e. measurable, μ(S) = 0 iff ν({w ≠ 0} ∩ S) = 0 (Mathlib withDensity_apply_eq_zero').
   - By Step 0, ν({w ≠ 0} ∩ S) = Hⁿ(({w ≠ 0} ∩ S) ∩ M).
   - Since w > 0 on M, ({w ≠ 0} ∩ S) ∩ M ⊆ M ∩ S and M ∩ S ⊆ ({w ≠ 0} ∩ S) ∩ M, so the two sets are equal.
   Therefore μ(S) = 0 iff Hⁿ(M ∩ S) = 0 (monotonicity of Hⁿ in both directions).

3. (c) Tangent planes. Let x ∈ ℝ^N and let P satisfy HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x P. The rank condition finrank P = n is the same in both predicates. Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N) and set
   F(r) := ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f(y)θ(x + r y) dHⁿ(y),
   G(r) := (rⁿ)⁻¹ ∫ f(η_{x,r}(y)) dμ(y).
   By hypothesis F(r) → θ(x)∫_P f dHⁿ as r ↓ 0. Fix r > 0 and write η := η_{x,r}.
   3a. ∫ f(η(y)) dμ(y) = ∫ w(z).toReal · f(η(z)) dν(z), by Mathlib integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul₀ (w is ν-a.e. measurable and finite). This equals ∫_M θ(z) f(η(z)) dHⁿ(z): by Step 0, at ν-a.e. z we have z ∈ M and w(z).toReal = θ(z), so the integrands agree ν-a.e. (integral_congr_ae).
   3b. Apply (A) to the set M and the function g(y) := f(y)θ(x + r y). This gives F(r) = (rⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_M f(η(z)) θ(x + r·η(z)) dHⁿ(z). For every z, x + r·η(z) = x + r·r⁻¹(z − x) = z (r ≠ 0), so the integrand is f(η(z))θ(z). By 3a, F(r) = (rⁿ)⁻¹ ∫ f(η(y)) dμ(y) = G(r). No integrability check is needed, because (A) holds for every g under the Bochner convention.
   3c. F and G agree on (0, ∞), which is a member of the filter 𝓝[>]0. Hence G(r) → θ(x)∫_P f dHⁿ as r ↓ 0 (Filter.Tendsto.congr'). Since f was arbitrary, HasApproxTangentPlaneWithMultiplicity n μ x P (θ x) holds.

4. Steps 1, 2 and 3 prove the three conjuncts. ∎
proof_key_steps: Substitute μ = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity(ofReal∘θ). The density w = ofReal∘θ is a.e.-measurable and finite, positive on M with w.toReal = θ on M, and a.e. point of Hⁿ⌞M lies in M.
(a) μ(K) = ∫_{M∩K} ofReal θ dHⁿ < ∞ by local integrability of θ.
(b) μ(S) = 0 ⟺ (Hⁿ⌞M)({w ≠ 0} ∩ S) = 0 ⟺ Hⁿ(M ∩ S) = 0, since w > 0 on M.
(c) For r > 0: (rⁿ)⁻¹∫ f∘η_{x,r} dμ = (rⁿ)⁻¹∫_M θ·f∘η_{x,r} dHⁿ = ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f(y)θ(x+ry) dHⁿ(y), by withDensity integration, child setIntegral_blowUpMap_image, and x + r·η_{x,r}(z) = z.
The two functions agree on (0,∞), so they have the same limit θ(x)∫_P f as r ↓ 0; the rank condition is shared.

audit.reason: All three conclusions and hypotheses match. Local integrability gives compact finiteness; a.e. measurability and positivity give the null-set equivalence for arbitrary S. The density integration formula and declared blow-up dependency prove tangent conversion. No x ∈ M assumption is needed for that implication. The proof is complete and non-circular.
